Explicit derivatives show the cost-normalized objective has exactly one maximizer, the positive-coefficient expansion of -log((1+sqrt(1-4z))/2) proves its price/monotonicity bounds, and uniform small-d plus matched c^2 scaling prove the endpoint laws. No computation is substituted for a quantified proof. The package contains a reproducing checker with 2,441 successful exact/numeric assertions.

value.rationale: Row-application cost heterogeneity naturally changes the work allocation in iterative linear solvers. The exact optimizing sampler is a nontrivial strict interior law, quantitatively connecting nearly orthogonal fair sampling to nearly parallel square-root-price sampling; the singular second-order correction identifies the scale on which expense affects the preferred row. This gives a meaningful benchmark for cost-aware stochastic projection while clearly excluding measured wall-clock gains.
